title: Carantania
capsule: Carantania was the first Slavic principality to emerge as a recognisable political entity, occupying the eastern Alps—roughly today's Carinthia and parts of Slovenia—from the mid-seventh century. Under pressure from the Avars, the Carantanians entered into alliance with the Bavarian dukes around 745, an association that drew them into the Carolingian sphere and initiated the Christianisation conducted by missionaries of the Archdiocese of Salzburg. Frankish overlordship increased until 828, when direct Carolingian administration replaced the local princes; Carantania became the nucleus of the later March of Carinthia, and its distinctive Slavic-language ducal inauguration ritual at the Prince's Stone survived as a ceremonial curiosity until 1414.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Carantania's general geographic setting is clear from Frankish annals, but the extent of the principality in its early decades before c. 743 is reconstructed from fragmentary sources and lacks hard boundary definition.
